extracted.intended_audience: HUD and USDA officials, state/local housing agencies, housing industry stakeholders (builders, developers), and attorneys/policy analysts
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register notice announcing the immediate rescission of HUD/USDA's Final Determination adopting updated energy-efficiency building codes, explaining statutory requirements, procedural history, factual bases considered (e.g., costs, data timeliness), litigation outcome, and the effect of the rescission.

rubrics_metrics.name: EISA adoption requirements for updated codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Following each update, HUD and USDA are required to adopt the new versions of the IECC and ASHRAE 90.1 within one year. If the one-year deadline is not met, the agencies may adopt updated versions only if they make a determination "that the revised codes do not negatively affect the availability or affordability" of the covered housing and the Secretary of Energy has determined "that the revised code or standard would improve energy efficiency."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets the statutory legal standard the agencies must satisfy to adopt updated model codes when the one-year window has passed: (1) a determination of no negative effect on availability/affordability, and (2) a separate Energy Secretary determination of improved energy efficiency. Agencies must therefore frame their analyses and findings to address both prongs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of IECC vs. ASHRAE 90.1
rubrics_metrics.description: The IECC standard applies to single family homes and multifamily low-rise buildings (up to 3 stories), while the ASHRAE 90.1 standard applies to multifamily residential buildings with 4 or more stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must apply the correct model code/standard based on building type and height when analyzing impacts and when issuing determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programs covered by EISA
rubrics_metrics.description: EISA applies to a list of HUD and USDA programs (Public Housing Capital Fund; Capital Fund Financing Program; HOPE VI; Choice Neighborhoods Implementation Grants; Project-Based Voucher Program; Section 202 Supportive Housing for the Elderly; Section 811 Supportive Housing for Persons with Disabilities; Rental Assistance Demonstration; FHA Single Family Mortgage Insurance Programs; FHA Multifamily Mortgage Insurance Programs; USDA Section 502 Guaranteed Housing Loans; USDA Section 502 Rural Direct Housing Loans; and USDA Section 523 Mutual Self Help Technical Assistance Grants, homeowner participants). For HUD, EISA also applies to new construction projects in the HOME Investment Partnerships Program and the Housing Trust Fund through program statutes or regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinations under EISA must identify and account for effects on these enumerated covered programs; analyses should be tailored to the program-specific contexts and statutory authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of economic analysis and public comments in determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD and USDA published a Preliminary Determination, received public comment, and later published a Final Determination with an updated economic analysis; the Final Determination made changes to the Preliminary Determination based on public comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should rely on and document transparent economic analyses and respond to substantive public comments; public comments can and should inform changes between preliminary and final determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and currency of data used in analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The agencies note that econometrics relied upon in the Preliminary Determination are from 2020 and 2021 (making them up to six years old) and that even the Final Determination's updated measures included numbers only through 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Currency of data is a material consideration in evaluating affordability impacts; agencies should use sufficiently up-to-date data to support their findings and explain any reliance on older data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors relevant to assessing negative effects on affordability/availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice identifies multiple factors that can exert upward pressure on housing construction costs and thus affect affordability/availability: building material cost increases (Producer Price Index spikes), contractor bid increases, supply chain issues, mortgage rate changes, land costs and appreciation, and alternative land uses (e.g., data center construction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses of whether revised codes negatively affect availability/affordability should consider a broad set of cost and market variables (materials, labor/contract bids, supply chains, financing costs, land prices and competing land uses) and support claims with empirical data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of §45L tax credit and other federal incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Determination overstated the availability of the §45L New Energy Tax Credit as a vehicle to offset costs; the §45L credit is not a direct subsidy for building to the 2021 IECC but is available to eligible contractors who construct or sell new homes meeting specific ENERGY STAR or DOE program standards; the credit amount varies based on energy savings and prevailing wage rates, and the IRA-related acceleration of sunset dates reduces its utility (§45L set to expire for homes acquired after June 30, 2026).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on tax credits or federal incentives to offset compliance costs, agencies must accurately characterize eligibility, magnitude, timing (sunset/expiration), and the extent to which those incentives directly apply to the code/standard at issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review and vulnerability under the Administrative Procedure Act
rubrics_metrics.description: A coalition sued HUD and USDA alleging that the 2024 Final Determination violates the Administrative Procedure Act, 5 U.S.C. 706; the court denied the Agencies' motion to dismiss and granted in part plaintiffs' summary judgment, setting aside and vacating the 2024 Final Determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency determinations under EISA must be legally defensible under APA standards; agencies should ensure record support, reasoned explanation, and procedural regularity to withstand judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect and timing of rescission
rubrics_metrics.description: This rescission is effective May 1, 2026. Effective immediately, HUD and USDA rescind the April 26, 2024 Final Determination in its entirety and rescind subsequent notices related to extensions of effective dates; each covered program shall comply with the energy efficiency standards that were in effect immediately prior to the publication of the Final Determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rescission returns covered programs to previously applicable standards as of immediately before the vacated Final Determination, and agencies must communicate effective dates and transitional requirements clearly to affected parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official publication and citation conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The official electronic format is the PDF on govinfo.gov; the XML rendition on FederalRegister.gov is a prototype and does not replace the official print version or the official electronic version on GPO’s govinfo.gov. Only official editions provide legal notice under 44 U.S.C. 1503 & 1507.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should rely on the official PDF/govinfo.gov for legal citation and notice determinations; the website's XML is informational and may not carry legal effect until ACFR grants official status.
